scope: Internal PostgreSQL immutable historical alias preparation, frozen latest hash-point reads and the existing report engine/pages; not a public contains implementation

validation.adversarialReview: Scoped Go from the independent external-plugin-developer reviewer for alias/latest preparation after sparse-array input validation was fixed; no approval of unfinished contains jobs or live installation browsing

budgets.note: Sorter budgets exclude caller lease/transaction overhead. Worker budgets include their control reserve. Physical plans are measured separately; these do not bound label bytes, disk IO, retries or wall-clock duration.

aliasSave.note: Excludes caller transaction/lease control; repeated identities use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, without updating existing versions.

frozenLatestPoints.note: Includes index-readiness result; empty matches perform zero SQL requests.

regressions: Missing metadata primary keys could scan 50,001 heads; requests and migration now fail before the publication join.
A broad bucket index caused 137 cohort candidates to be read and sorted for a32-row copy. Bucket and sort-input indexes now cover only their actual sections, with exact predicate readiness checks.
The former broad sort-input index also introduced a Sort for one recovered bucket (no overread in that one-row diagnostic). Final tests use two candidate buckets and assert one-row native seeks.
Prepared generic plans use the explicit fixed section predicate; no scan-method planner setting is forced.
Actual read-only PostgreSQL transactions reject an injected write with SQLSTATE25006; concurrent refresh and cleanup cannot split page metadata from its rows.
Former user and legacy username aliases retain their identity while lookup returns the same publication's latest event after a user change.
A captured source excludes later backdated appends, and the event-time cutoff excludes already-committed future rows from aliases and latest metadata together.
Injected alias insertion failure rolls back latest metadata and source advancement before recording terminal failure.
Repeated activity retains only distinct alias identities without an MVCC update to existing alias rows.
Sparse input arrays are rejected before storage access; missing or mismatched latest point rows fail instead of shortening a search result.
Default and prepared generic plans put publication, whole-period bucket and all 200 latest hash keys into the native index condition.

limits: All five section-page families exist only in the internal PostgreSQL implementation; public provider/HTTP/RPC/Console wiring is still pending.
Legacy50000-row runtime, optional eventPages and v1 prototype still await direct replacement. No backward-API compatibility approval.
Other-provider report engines, historical installation search, common maintenance, retry/recovery and bounded retention/expiry remain unfinished.
Previous merge passes remain stored; this slice does not implement their cleanup.
No raw event deletion, retention limit, new raw label-length limit or raw field rewrite.
Native plans describe these fixtures and SQL, not unconditional planner, byte-memory or throughput guarantees.
Final standalone E2E remains pending completion of the full implementation and the20GiB disk preflight; no threshold is bypassed.
Public historical contains reservation, immutable result ordering/cursors and base-publication retention references are not implemented by this alias slice.

The contains consumer must use a new current private storage revision and explicit recreation of unreleased derived state, excluding old alias-free or partly prepared jobs without compatibility markers.
Live all/exact installation browsing remains unfinished. The separate UTF-16 live-order probe is not shipped code or evidence that every legacy key will fit a PostgreSQL index.
